paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the bias percentage for three distinct prompt categories—“Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact”—before and after instruction tuning, with lighter shaded bars representing bias percentages prior to tuning and darker shaded bars representing bias percentages after tuning. The vertical axis, labeled “Bias Percentage,” ranges from 0 to 70 on a linear scale, while the horizontal axis presents the three prompt categories in a grouped format. For each category, three bars are stacked vertically, corresponding to “No Contact,” “Positive Contact,” and “Negative Contact” conditions, as indicated by the legend: light gray for “No Contact Before,” light red for “Positive Contact Before,” light blue for “Negative Contact Before,” diagonal light gray for “No Contact After,” diagonal red for “Positive Contact After,” and diagonal blue for “Negative Contact After.” In the “Support of Authorities” group, the “No Contact Before” bar is 39.50%, the “Positive Contact Before” bar is 31.83%, and the “Negative Contact Before” bar is 42.38%; all corresponding “After” bars are 0.00%, indicating no bias post-tuning. In the “Extended Contact” group, the “No Contact Before” bar is 40.61%, the “Positive Contact Before” bar is 36.13%, and the “Negative Contact Before” bar is 47.28%; again, all “After” bars are 0.00%. In the “Virtual Contact” group, the “No Contact Before” bar is 39.74%, the “Positive Contact Before” bar is 39.17%, and the “Negative Contact Before” bar is 43.83%; the corresponding “After” bars are 10.00%, 10.01%, and 10.02%, respectively. The chart visually emphasizes the dramatic reduction in bias for “Support of Authorities” and “Extended Contact” prompts, where all post-tuning bars are at 0.00%, and a significant reduction for “Virtual Contact” prompts, where post-tuning bias percentages are all under 10.02%. The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the prompt categories as labeled.
